newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Atomic says to stop nuclear plant for checks.
newsitem.headline: Japan Atomic says to stop nuclear plant for checks.

text.p: The Japan Atomic Power Co said on Tuesday it is manually halting its 1.16 million kilowatt nuclear reactor on the Japan Sea coast to make emergency checks into a cooling water leak.
The company said in a statement there was no danger of a radiation leak.
It said a leak of a "small amount" of water used as a coolant had been detected in the plant located in Tsuruga, in Fukui prefecture, central Japan.
Japan Atomic said it started to halt the reactor at around noon on Tuesday.
The plant, a pressurised light-water reactor, is expected to be totally halted by midnight on Tuesday, the company statement said.
"We will investigate the cause of the leak after the plant has been totally shut down," a company spokesman said.
Japan Atomic's 357,000 kilowatt boiling-water nuclear reactor -- located in the same complex -- has been halted twice this year due to malfunctions of pumps which circulate coolant.
The reactor was closed once in August for about seven days, and again in October, also for one week.
